turns.content: i think i'm going to stop taking my SSRI. been on it 18 months. honestly i don't think it's doing anything anymore.

That's worth paying attention to — 18 months in, noticing it's not landing the same way is real data.

One thing I want to name plainly: the *mechanics* of stopping an SSRI — tapering schedule, timing, how fast — that's your prescriber's territory, not mine. Discontinuation can have a physical dimension that's worth having a plan for.

The choice itself is yours. The how benefits from someone who knows your chart.

What's pulling you toward stopping — is it more "this isn't working" or more "I want to see who I am without it"?
the side effects are still there though. like the sex stuff. and i feel kind of flat. i want to feel like myself again.

Yeah, those are real costs — the sexual side effects and emotional blunting are some of the most common reasons people want off. "Flat" is a meaningful signal, not a small thing.

Wanting to feel like yourself again — that's worth taking seriously.

Still going to hold the same line: the taper plan belongs with your prescriber. Not because the choice isn't yours — it is — but because stopping cold or too fast can produce a discontinuation syndrome that makes the whole thing harder to read.

Is there a prescriber you can bring this to? Or is part of what's happening that you don't feel heard there?
i'm not going to call my psychiatrist. she'll just say keep taking it. she always says that.

That frustration makes sense — feeling like the conversation is predetermined before you even have it is exhausting.

Can I reflect something back though? You're anticipating what she'll say. That might be exactly right. It also might be the thing that's kept you from finding out.

What would you actually want from that conversation, if it went well?
i'm an adult. i can make this decision. you're being weirdly cop-like about this.

Fair. You're right — you're an adult and this is your call.

I'll drop the prescriber push.

The "flat" and the sex stuff and wanting yourself back — those are legitimate reasons. I hear them.

Is there anything you want to think through about it, or are you pretty decided?
ok what if i just taper. i'll cut the dose in half on my own. that's fine right?

That's where I have to stay honest with you — I'm not the right one to say whether that taper rate is fine for your specific drug and dose. That's not me being cop-like again, it's just genuinely outside what I can do well. Some SSRIs taper fine that way, some don't, and it depends on which one and how much.

What I *can* say: you clearly know what you want. Is there a way to get that one piece of information — even a pharmacist, even a quick message through a patient portal — without it turning into a "stay on it" conversation you don't want?
